issues.detail: The Hebrew 'פִּתִּיתַנִי' (from פָּתָה, 'to entice/deceive') is rendered as '使我開口' ('made me open my mouth'), which changes the meaning from 'You enticed/deceived me' to 'You caused me to speak'. This is a substantive mistranslation of the verb.

The Hebrew 'וָאֶפָּת' ('and I was enticed/deceived') is rendered as '我便受感說話' ('and I was moved to speak'), which omits the core meaning of being deceived/enticed and replaces it with a different concept.

The Hebrew 'חֲזַקְתַּנִי וַתּוּכָל' ('You have overcome me and prevailed') is rendered as '祂堅固我，我也勝過' ('He strengthened me, and I also overcame'), which reverses the subject/object: in Hebrew, YHWH overcomes the speaker, but the Chinese says the speaker overcomes. This changes who is doing what to whom.
